```{r}
#| include: false

library(knitr)
library(rmarkdown)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

theme_set(theme_minimal()+
          theme(strip.background =element_rect(fill="lightgray"),
                axis.title.x  = element_text(angle = 0,
                                            size = rel(1.5),
                                            margin = margin(10,0,0,0)),
                axis.title.y  = element_text(angle = 0,
                                            size = rel(1.5),
                                            margin = margin(0,10,0,0))
                )
          )
```

Let's analyze the `starwars` data:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
ice_cream <- read_csv("https://bcdanl.github.io/data/ben-and-jerry-cleaned.csv")
```


```{r}
#| results: asis
rmarkdown::paged_table(ice_cream) 
```
```{r}
# Ice Cream stats
ice_cream %>%
  summarise(
    mean_price = mean(priceper1, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_price = min(priceper1, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_price = max(priceper1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
# Ice Cream Count
flavor_desc <- ice_cream %>%
  count(flavor_descr) %>%
  arrange(-n)
```
```{r}
# Ice Cream Filter
ice_cream %>%
  filter(region == "West")
```
```{r}
# Group By
ice_cream %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_price = mean(priceper1, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_price = median(priceper1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  )
```

```{r}
# Regression Model
model <- lm(priceper1 ~ usecoup + household_size + region, data = ice_cream)
summary(model)
```
